title: Chunked Attention + DMA Cooperative Kernel Playbook
content:
Purpose:

This is a pragmatic playbook documenting experiments and micro-designs for: chunked-attention kernels that cooperate with an async DMA prefetcher, compact fused-op microkernels (rotary + add bias + qk scaling + mask), and page-aware scheduling heuristics for paged KV caches. The goal is a repeatable set of implementation patterns that improve tail latency for long-context workloads while keeping steady-state throughput high.

Context and motivation:

We have two competing pressures: (1) long-context chat/assistant requests create KV working sets larger than on-device memory, requiring paged KV; (2) per-request latency SLOs demand low tail latency even when pages must be fetched. Existing single-threaded prefetch + generic FlashAttention kernels are suboptimal because they either block on DMA or pay high register pressure when we try to interleave. This doc explores cooperative chunking and double-buffered kernels with explicit DMA handoff to overlap IO, compute, and KV page management.

High-level pattern (chunked-coop):

- Split a request into contiguous query blocks (chunk_size tokens) chosen by empirical latency/throughput frontier. Typical chunk_size tested: 32–128 tokens for 8k-64k contexts.
- For each chunk, schedule a prefetch of required KV pages via an async DMA stream using a lightweight page-descriptor batch.
- Launch a compute microkernel for the previous chunk while DMA completes for the next chunk (double-buffering). Use producer-consumer semaphore between host-side scheduler and kernel to ensure ordering without host thread spinning.
- Within the kernel, make a cheap page-presence check (per-lane) reading a compact page-table resident in L1 (small N-hot bitmap indexed by KV page id) to avoid crashing on missing pages and fallback to a safe slow path that stashes partial results and returns control to host for fetch+resume.

Microkernel design notes:

- Layout: pack Q,K,V tiles so that K/V pages for chunk N are coalesced per warp. Use warp-level fragments (each warp loads a contiguous tile of KV page). Page descriptor contains (page_id, device_ptr_hi32, stride_words) to minimize metadata overhead.
- Mixed-precision accumulation: use fp16 storage, fp32 accumulation for dot-products and MLP-like matmuls inside fused kernels where rounding matters (e.g., attention scores). Use tensor cores when chunk token lengths and head sizes align. Provide fallbacks if alignment mismatches.
- Fusion targets: rotary + q scaling + causal mask application + softmax affinity + dropout mask (if applicable) can be fused into a single loop for the chunk. This reduces memory traffic and synchronization. Implementation detail: compute rotary in-register, apply bias add and scale before writing into shared memory scratchpad for warpwise reduce.
- Register pressure: prefer loop-tiling so per-thread register usage stays < 64. When > 64 registers would be needed, split into multiple passes writing to an L2-resident ephemeral buffer to reduce register pressure. Microbenchmarks showed 8–12% latency regression but 20–30% drop in spilling.

DMA prefetcher and page descriptor batching:

- Use two CUDA streams: stream A (compute) and stream B (DMA). Enqueue batched cudaMemcpyAsync operations for the set of pages needed by chunk N+1. Ensure cudaMemcpyAsync uses a pinned host staging buffer if page fetch originates from host (private deployments). For NVMe->GPU paths, issue io_uring + GPUDirect when available.
- Page descriptor size tuned to ~32–64 bytes. Keep descriptors contiguous in a hot buffer that kernel can read via __ldg to get small-latency metadata.
- Backpressure: track outstanding page fetches <= max_outstanding_pages_per_context (tunable, default 8). If limit hit, scheduler should either (a) escalate to a higher-priority compute tier (dedicated pool), (b) throttle ingress, or (c) fall back to conservative blocking compute per chunk to avoid unbounded memory growth.

Scheduling heuristics and policy notes:

- Request scoring: priority = alpha * (remaining_tokens/avg_chunk) + beta * SLA_class + gamma * page_miss_probability. alpha,beta,gamma tuned from logs. Higher priority requests get earlier DMA scheduling and map to compute lanes with reserved warp-slots.
- Page coalescing: group DMA requests by NVMM locality and by model-shard to maximize throughput. Small pages (4–16KB) should be coalesced so DMA payloads are > 1MB to reduce PCIe overheads in remote deployments.

Fallback and correctness paths:

- Missing page during kernel: kernel writes partial accumulators to a small per-request staging area (in device DRAM) and returns an error code. Host runtime then blocks that request, issues necessary fetches, and relaunches kernel resuming from next chunk. Keep a small per-request resume-state with (chunk_idx, q_offset, partial_accum_ptr).
- Consistency: ensure page-version stamping. Every page descriptor carries a monotonic page_version. Kernel checks descriptor version when reading; if mismatch, go to fallback to avoid using stale KV. Version increments on writeback.

Profiling and microbench results (sanity numbers):

- Test bed: A100-40GB, pcie gen4 NVMe backing store (local), 16-head model, head_dim=64, sequence length 32k.
- Baseline (no chunked DMA, single FlashAttn kernel): median latency for 32k seq = 240ms, p99 = 860ms, throughput = 1200 tokens/s.
- Chunked double-buffered + fused microkernel (chunk=64): median = 170ms, p99 = 320ms, throughput = 1500 tokens/s.
- Tradeoffs observed: smaller chunk sizes reduce p99 but increase kernel-launch overheads and reduce throughput. chunk=32 p99 260ms but throughput drops ~8%. chunk=128 slightly improves throughput but p99 rises due to larger windows needing more pages.

Implementation checklist (next actionable tasks):

- [ ] Prototype page-descriptor ring buffer and kernel-side ldg reader (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Implement double-buffer launch harness with semaphores and unit-tests for resume path (owner: Ava).
- [ ] Wire page-version stamping into KV manager and expose API to kernel (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Create microbench harness that synthetically generates cold-page patterns and records p50/p95/p99 with trace markers (owner: Diego).

Open questions and risks:

- How to generalize to multi-GPU sharded KV where cross-GPU fetches are required? We may need a two-stage DMA (peer->host->peer) or RDMA-aware prefetcher with a rendezvous protocol.
- Interaction with garbage collection of KV pages: eviction during compute should be prevented by reference-counting pages used by running kernels.
- Safety/perf tuning for low-memory GPUs (24GB): chunking strategy might need to be much smaller or fall back to grouped re-evaluation scheduling.

Notes on related work and references:

- Inspiration: NVidia's async copy + double-buffer idioms in cuBLAS and Triton examples, FlashAttention's fusion strategies, and in-house paged KV experiments (see linked PR and Confluence).
- See linked_artifacts for initial PR and tracking ticket.

Appendix: quick pseudo-workflow

1) Scheduler computes chunk plan and page set for request.
2) Scheduler writes page descriptors to descriptor ring and issues cudaMemcpyAsync for device-resident copies.
3) Launch kernel for chunk 0 (no DMA overlap).
4) For each subsequent chunk i: kernel(i) computes while DMA for chunk i+1 progresses. On kernel exit, kernel signals host that it consumed buffer(i), host enqueues new DMA if any, and relaunches kernel(i+1) with new buffer index.
5) If kernel detects missing page, it writes resume info and returns error. Host fetches missing pages synchronously, then relaunches from resume point.

End of playbook.

Comments welcome — drop notes inline or ping #serving-runtime-kernel on Slack for synchronous follow-ups.
